Our second pick for Thursday night is Julian Lewis to go over 30.5 pass attempts as the Buffs take on Georgia Tech. However, this Colorado team will look a lot different from last year. 

Colorado brought in new offensive coordinator Brennan Marion who joins Prime's staff after coaching at Sac State. Before his stint leading the Hornets, Marion was widely known for designing the high-tempo "Go-Go" offense while serving as the offensive coordinator at UNLV which relies on high-tempo distribution, fast-paced decision making, and quick-trigger throws to keep defenses stretched.

The wide receiver room looks different as well with Danny Scudero joining from San Jose State  and DeAndre Moore Jr. from Texas. Kam Perry and Ernest Campbell also joined Colorado and should see significant playing time. Georgia Tech made a number of changes on the defensive side of the ball, but last season they struggled defending the pass ranking 114th in EPA per pass. 

One thing Colorado has not done well in the Sanders era is run the ball. Colorado finished near the bottom of the country in rushing efficiency last season and is breaking in a newly assembled offensive line. Sanders also said the plan is to rotate between 3-4 running backs in the game. If they struggle to get anything going on the ground it will force them to throw more often. 

Another reason to like Lewis is the potential game script. Colorado currently finds themselves around touchdown underdogs on Thursday which could force them to play catch up. 

With the additions at WR, the high-tempo style of OC Brennan Marions offense, and the potential game script, I think Lewis sees enough volume to clear this pass attempt line.

The biggest discount in fantasy is drafting criminals (or perceived ones).

& the NFL almost never makes a suspension before letting a case play out in court.

Josh Jacobs was RB6 in PPG (19.6) & RB3 in expected PPG (18.3) through WK10 last year – before suffering a knee contusion WK11. 

He was a 2/3 turn pick at the start of the offseason.

& he’s fallen to the 3/4 turn, to the 4/5 turn, now all the way into RD5 – all because of a *potential* suspension that isn’t likely to hit until next year.

It’s almost like nobody learned from the Rashee Rice situation last year….

Rice was suspended 6 games & fell all the way to RD6…. 

Some other RD6 picks (in ADP) last year?

- Isiah Pacheco
- Tony Pollard
- Aaron Jones
- Calvin Ridley
- TJ Hockenson
- Jerry Jeudy
- Travis Hunter

These are the players people drafted over Rashee Rice because they didn’t want to wait 6 games for a potential 2nd-half league-winner.

Jacobs is now falling into that same range – a range where most of the players picked are actually just going to suck…

Will Jacobs actually get suspended? This year? Who knows.

What we do know is Jacobs is a great bet to score fantasy points when active; he has averaged 15+ PPG in 5 of the last 6 seasons.

Getting him anytime after RD4 is a no-brainer.

These are the types of picks Championships are made of.
